messages:
Shreya: Heads up — timeline's slipping ~10–14 days. I want to propose a lightweight 'safety valve' so we can automatically carve a minimal launch slice and avoid last-minute scope fights. :eyes:
Devin: +1. Can you sketch what you mean by 'safety valve'? automated cuts or manual sign-off?
Shreya: Prefer automated guardrails with explicit criteria. If we hit X (e.g. >5 severity-1 bugs OR infra latency regression >20% OR pilot opt-in <70%) then auto-fallback to MVP-slim. Keeps PM/ENG alignment when pressure hits.
Kevin: Leaning towards a combination: auto-detectors for obvious failures + human override. We should list what gets cut automatically vs what requires manual.
Amy: Agreed. Suggested auto-cut candidates: non-essential UX polish, advanced tenant routing, experiments (A/B variants), analytics-per-route. Keep core flows: auth, core generation, cost controls.
Omar: Quick note — Dedicated infra quotas might be the limiter. If we cut features that reduce GPU memory but add latency, we could make things worse. Need to model perf impact per cut.
Devin: Here's a tiny starter matrix (can expand in doc):
```
auto_cut_condition | feature_to_cut           | owner
-------------------|--------------------------|------
perf > +20%        | multi-tenant routing     | Kevin
bugs >=5 sev1      | prompt-editor UX         | Amy
pilot < 70%        | advanced telemetry/event | Omar
```
Shreya: Perfect. Let's also include launch buckets: MVP (must ship), MVP+ (nice-to-have if green), v1 (post-launch). We should tag each ticket with bucket label so cut decisions are mechanically enforceable.
Kevin: I can run a quick impact calcs for the top 10 candidate cuts by EOD — latency, cost delta, user-facing regressions. Will post a summary table. :+1:
Amy: I'll start labeling tickets and mark the ones with hidden infra risks. Also propose we set a canary release window: 48h canary, then open to 20% traffic, then full. If any safety valve triggers during canary -> rollback and apply cutlist.
release-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-start at 2026-04-10T15:00Z (auto-notify on failures).
Omar: Can we add a criterion: telemetry signal quality must be within 90% of expected to count canary as valid. If telemetry is noisy, we treat as fail-safe and hold.
Devin: Good call. That avoids false passes.
Shreya: Decisions so far: 1) implement safety-valve with both auto and manual gates; 2) tag tickets as MVP / MVP+ / v1; 3) canary window + rollback policy; 4) owners: Kevin (impact calcs), Amy (ticket labels), Omar (telemetry guard).
Kevin: I'll drop the impact calcs doc link here when ready.
Amy: Labeling started. ETA for full labels: tomorrow morning.
Shreya: I'll update the launch checklist and add the safety-valve runbook (steps to flip manual override, where to find cut matrix). Assigning follow-ups in the doc. @Kevin @Amy @Omar please ping if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
Devin: Thanks — this should keep scope negotiations from derailing the timeline.
Shreya: One more — propose we publish a short note to stakeholders summarizing the cut buckets and the safety valve rules so expectations are clear before freeze. I'll draft and share by EOD.
Kevin: 👍
Amy: 👍
Omar: 👍
Shreya: Draft posted: https://redwood.atlassian.org/launch/safety-valve (internal). Feedback welcome.
